December, 1991    Page Reply

 How to write to us...02     -

 Derek Burn...........03    04

 John Saunders........05    08

 Malcolm Perry........10    17

 Dennis Turton........18    20

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: Derek Burn, BUCKS.

Dear Ron and Brian,

Having just read the glowing
review of the new word processor
STYLE-WRITER in OUTLET issue 51,
I would like to order a copy. It
certainly sounds as though it
may be the word processor that
the Coupe has been waiting for
although I have to say that I am
finding OUTWRITE very easy to
get on with.

I am a little sorry to see that
STYLE-WRITER doesn't include two
particular features without
which no self-respecting word
processor can consider itself
truly 'with it' - a 'mail-merge'
facility and a spell checker.

Perhaps there is no room even in
the 512K machine. Maybe these
could be made available later as
an optional extra for those with
the IMB memory extension?

                   Derek Burn

I'd be interested to know what
specific job the home user would
do with a mail-merge facility as
I can't think of a use other
than with a large company in a
"personalised" mailshot.

A simple spellchecker should not
be too hard to program although
typing the dictionary would be
hard work!It could also work for
OUTWRITE,STYLEWRITER and TASWORD
since the files are the same.
I just need time!       - Brian

From: John Saunders, BUCKS

Dear Chezron,

        Re: OUTWRITE 1.2
I was very interested in the
small mod. printed in OUTLET
purporting to give a contrasting
colour to the cursor in our w-p,
which I use quite a lot wherein
I do in fact lose the cursor
from time to time.

I have been unsuccessful with
the mod., perhaps because there
is no line 2200 to which to add.
I have tried adding the
recommended info to line 200; to
line 220 (a 'vacant' line), and
also to making line 200 with the
additions, into 220.

All this has not worked, but has
corrupted the program in some
way or other. What did work, on
one occasion, was as follows:

Add line 190 as advised:
Add to line 200 as advised for
    2200:
Move line 200 to 220 and delete
    200:
Run the prog - to result in a
    blank screen with no key
    reaction, except
Break to BASIC and then delete
    line 190 and revert to
    original line 200.
Then RUN.

Although this gave the desired
result on the one occasion, I
wold have been quite unable to
repeat it, and am at a loss.

Can you perhaps let me know if
there is a mistake in the OUTLET
article and if so you may care
to put a correction in the next
issue.

Another possibility occurs to me
- have you up-dated OUTWRITE
beyond the version I have?

           Yours etc.,

          John Saunders

Brian Cavers to John Saunders

A thousand apologies, John. I
pride myself on double-checking
any short programming tips
because I know how frustrating
it can be trying to get them to
work if there's an error.

Yes,line 2200 should be 200 but
the rest of it is O.K. because
I've just typed it in and it
works fine. My guess is you may
have mis-typed one of the POKEs.
Double-check them. You may have
assumed that they were 66499 and
66500, i.e., in sequence whereas
the second address is 66504. If
you POKE a wrong address,load
OUTWRITE again - don't just put
in the correct POKE.

If you have saved your previous
try you may have saved the
corruption. Does OUTWRITE work
O.K. now without the POKEs?

Make sure that OUTWRITE has all
fully loaded before breaking in
because if the code is not all
present you are likely to get a
crash.

You have the current version 1.2
so it must work unless you have
made any other changes.

Let me know if you still can't
get it to run properly and tell
me your exact colour settings
and the exact symptoms of the
corruption.
                        - Brian

From Malcolm Perry,KIDDERMINSTER


Re: All Format Show, Birmingham.

November 10th gave a choice:stay
at home for roast lunch and
watch Batman on TV or spend `4
(`3 if your Format arrived in
time) and visit the show. I had
made my mind up I was not going
but 11 AM sunday I decided
otherwise. Suffice to say I was
back in time to see Batman and
ate my packed lunch at home.

It should have been called "All
Formats Except Spectrum"!O.K.,to
be fair there were the odd
Spectrum bits and pieces if you
looked hard enough.

General hardware such as discs,
labels, paper, ribbons etc., in
ample supply and prices between
cheap and not-so-cheap. There
were plenty of various firms
showing off their computers and
bags of software for all but
Spectrums. Empty tables were
conspicious by their numbers.

However on the Spectrum/Sam
scene Samco was represented
selling games and the usual sam
utilities with a Sam box on
display but no Sam in sight. I
would have thought a demo and
try-out of the games being sold
would have,at least,been a must
(perhaps they had such a rush in
the morning they had sold the
demo model by midday!!!).

FORMAT had the usual stand. SAM
SUPPLEMENT and ZAT were demon-
strating their discs on Sams and
that was all I spotted! There
were odd +2's,+3's and Interface
1's to be found but not much
else was seen of interest. You
could buy a +2 circuit and
service booklet for `5 but I had
bought mine the week before at a
radio show for only `2.My journ-
ey was not a total loss as I
managed to replace my bottle of
disc-cleaning fluid that had
evaporated into thin air 'cos I
did not put the top back on
properly, for 50p (only seen in
packs with disc before). I also
got a 6-way Centronics automatic
printer switch that was sorely
needed when running four systems
and only having a 2-way switch.

I can strongly recommend auto-
matic switches when running
multiple computers and only one
printer (PSST.... anybody wanna
buy a 2-way?).

When I arrived about midday it
was quite crowded in the halls
but an hour later it had thinned
out quite a bit. I possibly
missed some "bargains" by not
getting there earlier but from
the type of stalls present I
would not think much in my line.

If you are reading this then
your interests most likely would
not have been catered for. On
top of this the poor way this
aspect of computing was suported
by traders would not be too
likely to gain new recruits.

Say someone was thinking of a
computer. They would see a
couple of Sams with a disc demo/
mag. and little else related
with Sam. Brand x has many
stalls with working computers
showing off their wares with a
fair selection of software and
hardware. Which is going to draw
the most interest? Which is
going to make people stop and
look? a box with a picture of
SAM or a number of working
computers running both serious
programs, demos and games?

I think part of the problem is
the entrance fee is too high.
This reflects on attendance and
so dealers do not consider it
worthwhile going.

At this type of show,rather than
each product-supplier having
their own space, would it not be
be better to book say,six tables
and then all Spectrum and Sam
products would be put on show.


Suppliers could take turns to
man the combined effort display.
O.K., so Mr X might whinge at
selling Mr Y's competitive
product but in the long run
prospective users would at least
see there is more to Sam than
two disc mags and a few games
and that Spectrums are still
well supported.

This would benefit all in the
long run.

Amateur radio-type shows are
mainly put on by local clubs. I
wonder if this idea would work
for computers with Sam and
Spectrum dealers working with
local clubs to put on a show?
This would ease the problems of
small supporters of the Sam and
Spectrum (which really covers a
fair proportion of software and
hardware suppliers) who would
not then have the full expense
of a stand and have to be tied
up manning stands at each show.

This column has been as inform-
ative and interesting on the
latest developments and up-and-
coming-items for the Spectrum
and Sam as the Birmingham
computer show was! All I can say
is, "Sorry!!".   - Malcolm Perry

Brian Cavers to Malcom Perry

We have difficulty finding time
to attend these fairs and we're
not encouraged by the attendance
of SAM and Spectrum users or at
least, the inability to know
which fairs may be well-attended
and which not.

It's not too bad for the box-
shifters who don't need to speak
much but we could talk ourselves
hoarse for 20 or 30 minutes
demonstrating say, OUTLET or
OUTWRITE for a sale of only `2
or `8 respectively. This is not
really economic except as promo-
tion so it becomes more and more
of an effort to go when we have
so many pressing tasks to do in
the production of OUTLET. -Brian

From Dennis A. Turton, LIVERPOOL

 RE: STANDING ORDERS.

Dear Ron & Brian,

What an excellent 50th edition
of OUTLET. Congratulations!

Now down to business. In your
letter to me in the form of an
ORDER FORM, you state that the
Standing Order charge is `3.50
per issue. My question is, is
this the price for the Spectrum
+3 disk version? If it is then
please send me a Standing Order
Form right away!

If this is right, how do you do
it for that price?

Whilst on the subject of Order
Forms, what fonts or program did
you use to obtain the lettering
that you use to produce the form
i.e, the heading at the top of
the form?I am also interested in
how the boxes are drawn,assuming
they were drawn on a Spectrum.
If this was not the case, do you
have such a program that will
draw lines across and down the
page? For example, designing and
drawing charts,e.g.,time tables.
I'm sure other people would find
this kind of utility very
useful.

Well, Ron & Brian, keep up the
brilliant work and here's to the
100th edition in December 1995!
                 - Dennis Turton

Brian Cavers to Dennis Turton

I'm afraid the +3 version of
OUTLET is NOT `3.50 by standing
order as you say: IT'S ONLY `3!!
Look carefully again at the form
and you will see all versions
are the same except microdrive.

Yes, `3 for the +3 version of
OUTLET is unbelievable isn't it?
You can still pay `4 for a blank
3"disc in some High Street shops
so how do we do it? By buying 3"
discs in bulk we can get them
for under `2. Remember, High St.
shops exist primarily for profit
with the customer as a means to
that end. We work the other way
round to produce something we
think is worthwhile and provide
a service with profit secondary.

It's a funny old world though.In
this same issue is a letter from
another reader, Marc Broster,who
rarely buys OUTLET because "at
`2 I don't think it's very good
value.", he says. Marc must have
bought an odd issue at one of
the All-Format Fairs where we
sell OUTLET at a ludicrous `2 so
he assumes that's the regular
price.I hope everyone will still
write to me at the funny farm
when they come to take me away.

Anyway, by now you should have
received the standing order form
Dennis. As for the order form,it
is done by a commercial printer
which accounts for the quality.
To integrate boxes and lines
with text you really need PCG'S
DTP package...

This comprises WORDMASTER,a word
processor, HEADLINER, a graphic
and title designer and TYPELINER
the "desktop publisher". They're
available separately or together
as follows...

           +D/DISCIPLE  +3/TAPE

 WORDMASTER   `13.95    `15.95

 HEADLINER    `10.95    `12.95

 TYPELINER    `18.95    `20.95

 ALL THREE    `37.95    `39.95


Free U.K. delivery from P.C.G.,
61 School Street, Barrow-in-
Furness, Cumbria, LA14 1EW

However, I note what you say
about drawing charts etc. and
these are usually programs that
are special to one task. For
instance we had a bar chart pro-
gram in Issue 50 called HI-BAR
and there's a graph chart soon
in a future issue. If you can
specify a particular task in
more detail then a reader may be
able to take on the project. If
simple, like HI-BAR, I may find
time myself. It should not be
too difficult to do something
like a timetable.

                        - Brian

From Alan D.Cox, DYFED, WALES


Dear Ron & Brian,

Do you know anything recent of
Ian Vaudrey? - you've mentioned
him once or twice in OUTLET I
think.I sent him an old Spectrum
for repair some while ago and
have had no response.

I note Malcolm Perry's comments
on the 'obscure' SCART
connections. I assume he was
commenting on my earlier letter,
but as I have pointed out, this
didn't appear in the SAM
version. I am therefore worried
about the suggestion of
definitely distinct editions.

I don't know what the solution
to your dilemma is, but I should
be unhappy to opt for one or the
other - I'm interested in both
(but don't really want to pay
double!)

        Yours sincerely,

           Alan D. Cox

Brian Cavers to Alan D. Cox

When the SAM and Spectrum OUTLET
versions were "overlapping" we
got several requests to separate
them. Now they are separate we
are getting requests from other
readers to "overlap"!Perhaps the
answer is to put the Spectrum
letters in the SAM ADDENDERS and
vice-versa (I think someone may
have already suggested that).

I was always happy for them to
be "merged" as one. I regard the
SAM as a Spectrum "PLUS" anyway.
It is easier for me to swap
files between SAM and Spectrum
via my Disciple than it is
between my Spectrum Disciple
set-up and my +3!

I wonder how it would have been
regarded if Clive Sinclair had
not sold out to Amstrad and had
produced the SAM under the name
Spectrum +4 with a Spectrum ROM
built in as well as the SAM ROM!
With Lord Clive's (sorry, SIR
Clive's) name and greater
resources plus TOTAL compatibil-
ity, the +4 would have dominated
the market or at least have got
the respect it deserved from the
media.

Regarding Ian Vaudrey's repair
service, I wrote to him and he
reports...

"[Mr.Cox's] machine was not just
sent for repair,he also enclosed
a "magic button" kit (PCW) which
I'd offered to try and install.

"For this reason I asked Mr. Cox
not to enclose any payment as I
would advise him of the cost
when I found out what the
installation entailed.

"I completed the repair to the
machine two days after receipt
and then I tried to obtain some
info about the kit by writing
and 'phoning various contacts
[without success].

"I wrote a letter to Mr. Cox and
requested the standard repair
charge of `16.90. Two days later
I got an inquiry from Mr. Cox
and thought at the time that our
letters must have crossed in the
post but I now suspect MY letter
didn't get mailed.

"I have now returned the machine
repaired for half price, `8.45.
                 - Ian Vaudrey"

The lesson from this is that if
ANYONE has ANY problem with ANY
mail order service, ALWAYS send
AT LEAST TWO FURTHER letters of
inquiry before taking action or
complaining publicly. Ian went
out of his way to help and only
made a single error (not mailing
a letter and even this is in
doubt - it could have got lost
in the post). If you order goods
by mail order and receive no
reply,write at least TWICE again
and allow at least two weeks
after the last attempt before
taking any action as we are all
human!                  - Brian

From: Simon Greenfield, LINCS



Dear Ron and Brian,

It truly amazes me how you keep
up not only the high standard of
each OUTLET produced, but that
you show a great deal of care
and understanding towards us,
your readers, overall, what with
the customer care service
payment for articles, items,
reviews etc, and with helping us
out with our every day to day
computer related problems, not
to mention replacing lost items.
I've said it before and I'll say
it again, you at Chezron are a
Godsend to us all, well done.

Just the other day, I received
the latest five-page SAMCO
newsletter, and read Alan Miles
new proposed customer type care
that they will be employing from
now on,regarding what's on offer
and when it will be available.


I can't help but feel if this is
perhaps Alan Miles responding to
the comments over the SAMCO
rodent that I was going on about
last time, which you replied to
in Issue 49, and said that you
had passed onto SAMCO. At the
time you said you were still
awaiting a reply from them?? I
hope it is and that it's the
beginning of a better service.

Whilst I'm on the subject of
Issue 49, it appears that when
you edited my letter, you made a
rather severe cock-up over my
quote from Alan Miles from the
newsletter that announced the
Sam mouse. Where I said "...the
ASIC chip..." you typed "...the
BASIC chip..." which in somebody
reading that must have inspired
the thought "what is this Green-
field geezer going on about,
quoting something somebody said
then typing "...BASIC..."
instead of "...ASIC..."???!!!

I know I never made the mis-type
because I kept the original text
file of that particular letter
and it checks o.k. so it's over
to you!

Also my little conversation with
SAMCO at the time regarding the
rep who quite blatantly told me
over the phone when I queried it
to him as to whether or not
existing versions of FLASH would
still be compatible with the new
mouse and who told me THAT THEY
WOULD BE, where I put it in the
sentence you seemed to have
omitted it, so again it read
oddly.

I'm not having a stab at you -
just asking next time to be a
bit more careful when editing
people's letters. No doubt it
was a case of pressures of being
over-worked that got to you, so
I forgive you seeing as you're
an excellent caring sort of
person?

You might like to let the
majority of your readership know
that good ol' Micro Mart are
covering the SAM in depth now as
they apparently have their very
own SAM-related columnist who
will be keeping tabs on Sammy's
babe from now on. It's good to
see that unlike that total waste
of trees publication 'NEW 16 BIT
EXPRESS' or was it 'NEW 16 BIT
COMMODORE CRAP EXPRESS'?? that
they are unbiased in their
opinions of other machines.

Twice this year I've written to
N.C.E 's letters columnist,
Mr. Hayden-Fitz-Williams in
support of our beloved SAM. The
first time they cannibalised my
letter of some three pages

letting him know what was what,
down to a paltry dozen or so
lines.

The second time I wrote correct-
ing this so called "FIRST FOR
THE NEWS"??!! weekly over their
announcement of three certain
SAM items which all had the
prices published wrongly, never
appeared in print, probably
lobbed in the bin?


I've noticed with them that if
you write in anything 16-bit
related to the letters page then
you win a fiver, but correct
them over things like the SAM
and what it can do and what's
available, and you get zilch!!

They should practice what they
preach on moralities to people.

It's a crying shame that the one
and only decent weekly computer
news mag, POPULAR COMPUTING
WEEKLY, went out of publication.
Pity it was not the pathetic NCE
instead of POP weekly. If FUTURE
publications had any sense they
would dump them where they
belong..RIGHT DOWN THE...

What happened to the "LOOK-A-
HEAD" column in Issue 50 please?
As it appeared to be missing,
and there must have been at
least 60+ free K's on the disk!!
It's always nice to know what we
can look forward to each coming
month in OUTLET.

Have you spotted SAMCO's
deliberate mistake in the latest
newsletter regarding the price
of the new music-making program,
'THE SOUND MACHINE'? They have
quoted it in the letter as
`9.99, but on the order form as
`14.99??!!

   Cheers, best regards to all

         Si Greenfield.

PS. MASTERBASIC is a must!.

Brian Cavers to Simon Greenfield

Thanks, Simon. Sorry about the
ASIC mis-typing but you have to
realize that much of the text we
receive has odd expressions that
are peculiar to the writer and
words are clipped either by the
writer or one of our many conv-
ersion programs. In this light,
it is easy for one of us to
think ASIC was a mis-spelling of
BASIC (we commonly see words
clipped in just that way).

Also, because, as I say, many
readers use their own odd
expressions, when I came to
check the text later I must have
thought you meant something like
"THE BASIC ROM CHIP".

Please believe me, we cannot be
more careful than we are!Text is
always double-checked but mostly
triple-checked and sometimes
more. To go further would be
impractical and we all must
accept errors from time to time.

The omission of your comment on
SAMCO may have been my being
cautious about criticism as it
can cause friction (and has!)
between us and other important
commercial contacts. In a severe
case, of course, we risk
litigation which could close us
down as we have few resources
for the cost of any such action.
All readers must accept that we
may cut out comments as we think
fit and must err on the side of
caution.

It's easy to think that we can
say what we like but we can't;we
have to take the same care as
any other publisher.However,with
no access to legal expertise we
have to be ultra-cautious!

Your letter is nowhere near this
extreme but it does explain why
we sometimes cut things (apart
from lack of space). Anyway, you
can always appeal as you have
done! We DO listen, as NCE did
not appear to do!

I also wrote to NCE following
publication of a letter therein
which said there was no software
for SAM. I listed much of the
software that WAS available but
they ignored MY letter!

Yes, that was annoying. I think
they owed it to their readers to
put the other side of the story.

As for their cannabalising your
lengthy letter, I think that was
understandable. We also have to
hack and slay some of the novels
we receive! They, like us, only
have so much room and you stand
more chance of publication when
writing to ANY periodical if you
are VERY concise.

LOOKAHEAD has been dropped from
the SAM version of OUTLET as it
refers only to Spectrum material
and several readers want the two
versions to be separate. The SAM
version is not compiled as far
ahead as the Spectrum one.

I may consider resurrecting it
as a sort of "what's-in-the-pipe
line" section meaning what MAY
appear over the next few issues.

                        - Brian

From Bob Wilkinson, PETERBOROUGH

Note that the COMET assembler by
Edwin Blink (from SAMCo) "locks
up" during assembly if FIND has
been previously used on a 14-
character label (and FIND fails
also in that situation). The
solution is to limit yourself to
13-character labels which is
generous anyway and always save
the source before assembly.

Also, be aware that COMET will
lock up during assembly if there
is a SLASH in a label.
                - Bob  Wilkinson


Thanks, Bob. Glad you backed up
the OUTWRITE source! Keep at it!
                         - Brian.

Твое письмо, конечно, далеко от подобных крайностей, но это объясняет, почему мы порой что-то вырезаем (помимо банальной нехватки места). Впрочем, ты всегда можешь подать апелляцию, как сейчас и сделал! МЫ-ТО прислушиваемся, чего об NCE, похоже, сказать нельзя!

Я тоже написал в NCE после публикации у них письма, где утверждалось, будто под SAM нет софта. Я перечислил внушительный список программ, которые БЫЛИ доступны, но они МОЕ письмо попросту проигнорировали!

Да, это было неприятно. Я считаю, они были обязаны перед своими читателями представить и противоположную точку зрения.

Что касается того, что они покромсали твое пространное письмо, думаю, это вполне понятно. Нам тоже приходится рубить и кромсать некоторые «романы», которые мы получаем! У них, как и у нас, место строго ограничено, и у вас гораздо больше шансов на публикацию в ЛЮБОМ периодическом издании, если вы пишите ОЧЕНЬ кратко.

Рубрика LOOKAHEAD была убрана из SAM-версии OUTLET, поскольку она относится исключительно к материалам для Spectrum, а некоторые читатели просили разделить эти две версии. Кроме того, SAM-версия не планируется настолько наперед, как спектрумовская.

Возможно, я подумаю о ее возрождении в виде раздела вроде «в планах», где будет рассказываться о том, что МОЖЕТ появиться в следующих нескольких номерах.
